author_or_org: Sajal Regmi, Siddhartha Pudasaini, Chetan Phakami Pun

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The study placed 100 memory-equipped LLM agents in charge of a closed, money-conserving spatial economy on real Pokhara Lakeside geography, where they earned wages, ran businesses, and set prices, simulating up to 26 simulated weeks.
claims.quote: We placed 100 memory-equipped large language model (LLM) agents in charge of a closed, money-conserving spatial economy on real Pokhara Lakeside geography (earning wages, running businesses, setting prices) and ran this multi-agent simulation for up to 26 simulated weeks, well past the 1-2 weeks typical of agent-society studies.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The simulation produced 91 validated runs with 2.44M agent decisions and 21.5B tokens; money stopped moving in a specific measurable way.
claims.quote: Across 91 validated runs (2.44M agent decisions, 21.5B tokens), the money stops moving, in a specific and measurable way.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A 12x tourist demand shock raised business revenue 4.62x (p<0.001), decomposed into a 1.50x extensive margin and a 3.07x intensive margin; wages moved 1.03x (p=0.42) and only 0.3% of 3,981 menu items were ever repriced (p=0.47).
claims.quote: A 12x tourist demand shock raises business revenue 4.62x (p<0.001), which we decompose exactly into a 1.50x extensive margin (more businesses trading) and a 3.07x intensive margin (more revenue each). Monetary transmission stops there. Wages move 1.03x (p=0.42); 0.3% of 3,981 menu items are ever repriced (p=0.47).

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A randomized cash transfer of NPR 5,000 to 20 of 100 agents left 96.7% still held 311 pulses later, with marginal propensity to consume 3-4%, indistinguishable from zero.
claims.quote: A randomized cash transfer (NPR 5,000 to 20 of 100 agents) shows the same pattern from the opposite direction: 96.7% is still held 311 pulses later, marginal propensity to consume 3-4% by two independent measures, indistinguishable from zero.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Wealth distribution was near-frozen at ρ=0.964 over 2 simulated weeks but not frozen, falling to 0.832 at 12 weeks and 0.752 at 26 weeks, showing horizon-dependence invisible to short studies.
claims.quote: The wealth distribution is consequently near-frozen at the horizon this literature uses (ρ=0.964over 2 simulated weeks), but not frozen. ρfalls to 0.832 at 12 weeks and 0.752 at 26, a horizon-dependence no short study can see.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Matched ablations showed swapping the backing LLM moved every measured outcome (p=0.0039), while deleting agents' memory moved none detectably.
claims.quote: Matched ablations show which knob actually matters. Swapping the backing LLM moves every outcome we measure (p=0.0039); deleting agents' memory moves none of them detectably.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: A purely social tool failed 94-97% of the time across two model families, against about 96% success on economic tools, with no measurable shift away from it.
claims.quote: A purely social tool fails 94-97% of the time across two model families, compared with ~96% success on economic tools, with no measurable shift away from it.
